name: Bright Magenta
lede: Bright Magenta is a modifier on [[magenta]], a vivid purplish pink that our sources record only in the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey.

sections.title: A survey name, not a system name
sections.body:
Unlike many bright- compounds, this one carries no other record in our sources: no CSS keyword, no ISCC-NBS block, no paint-brand plate behind it [1]. It is simply modifier grammar, bright plus magenta, collected when online volunteers typed color names for hex swatches in 2010 [1].

The word it modifies is older. Magenta began as a nickname for fuchsine, the aniline red dye of 1859, named for the Italian town where the French defeated the Austrians that June [4]. Ball describes the dye as a deep red, far from this screen pink-purple, so the swatch is not the history [4].

Its closest named neighbor is magenta itself, only 3.1 units away and read as more vivid still [2]. [[hot-magenta|Hot Magenta]] sits at 3.9, duller by comparison, and [[purple-pizzazz|Purple Pizzazz]] a little further out on the same side [2]. [[pinky-purple|Pink Purple]] sits further out too, duller than this swatch [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color within six units of this one over at least five percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A match would be a screen comparison with photographed, varnished paint, not a pigment test [3].
